newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian rail workers vow to continue strike.
newsitem.headline: Croatian rail workers vow to continue strike.

text.p: Croatian railway workers vowed on Monday to press ahead with a strike and rejected the government's claim it could not meet their demands for higher wages, local media reported.
Railway union leader Zlatko Pavletic insisted Croatian railways (HZ) had sufficient funds to give railway workers a raise, the state news agency HINA reported.
"We believe HZ has internal reserves to increase our wages," HINA quoted Pavletic as saying.
He said strikers would set up a strike fund as their protest could last for a long time.
Some 11,000 workers paralysed rail traffic across Croatia for the fifth day, halting 80 percent of services. International and some cargo trains continued to operate.
Rail workers accused HZ of putting pressure on the strikers.
"HZ has sent its controllers to all railway stations to threaten workers to sign a statement against the strike or be sacked," said a union statement quoted by HINA.
The head of Croatian railways, Marijan Klaric, told independent Radio 101 that HZ lacked funds to meet the workers' demands.
"We have no means to meet any (strikers') demands,"he said.
The loss-making HZ is subsidised by the state. Management said on Monday the government had refused to provide it with extra funds for wage increases.
Apart from public funds, HZ has used 33 million kuna ($6.1 million) from its 1996 earnings to pay salaries, the company said in a statement.
HZ said that due to daily losses of 1.6 million kuna ($300,000) caused by the strike, workers might not receive their November salaries.
It also denied it had threatened to sack all workers who ignored its demand to go back to work.

"HZ is not intimidating strikers and has no intention to sack anyone...But it has a (legal) right to reduce workers' wages for the working hours they spent striking," a HZ statement broadcast by state radio said. (1$= 5.44 kuna)
